detailed_rationale:
FY26 (year ended Mar-2026) print was strong on headline growth: consolidated revenue Rs 16,402.7cr / $1,870M, +35.9% YoY in INR, +29.2% YoY in USD; EBIT margin expanded 370bps YoY to 14.4%; Q4FY26 alone did Rs 4,450cr revenue (+30% YoY) at a 16.6% EBIT margin (highest-ever quarterly) and 20.6% EBITDA margin (+340bps YoY). A large share of FY26's growth was organic execution of the Sabre mega-deal -- management described itself as 'very comfortable' with delivery against the Sabre roadmap into CY2026, and ramp costs came in lower than planned (a genuine positive execution signal, not just a revenue headline). The company enters FY27 with a record $1.75bn executable order book (next-12-month book was $1.72bn at Q3FY26, +30% YoY, on 6 large deals that quarter spread across BFSI/healthcare/travel/Govt/insurance) -- healthy, diversified booking momentum, not one client carrying the number. [DATA -- one-off check, required by V1 protocol]: FY26 PAT of Rs 1,555.7cr (+91.6% YoY, far outpacing the 29.2% USD revenue growth) included a Rs 244cr deferred-tax credit (Rs 153cr of it landed in Q4FY26 alone), a reversal tied to the Cigniti-merger DTA/DTL structure -- not a recurring cash-earnings item. Stripping it out, 'clean' FY26 PAT is closer to Rs 1,311.7cr, i.e. underlying PAT growth is roughly 61-62% YoY rather than the headline 91.6%, and clean TTM EPS is meaningfully lower than the reported number -- the headline profit beat is real operationally but partly a tax-line artifact. Management itself guides the effective tax rate normalizing back to 23-24% by FY27-28 as the DTA runs off, so FY27 reported PAT growth will look structurally slower even before any Encora effect. FY27 guidance (given at the Q4FY26 print, well before Q1 FY27 numbers) is 13% constant-currency organic growth plus >20.5-21% consolidated EBITDA margin -- a deceleration in stated ambition versus FY26's realized 29.2%, though Coforge has a multi-year pattern of guiding conservatively and beating (FY26 is the latest example). As of this review (20-Jul-2026), Q1 FY27 results are NOT yet out: the board meets 27-Jul-2026 to approve them, with the analyst call on 28-Jul-2026 -- so the constant-currency growth actually delivered, TCV booked, and margin trajectory for the quarter cannot yet be checked against the 13% guide.

The dominant new structural fact is the Encora Digital acquisition: a $2.35bn enterprise-value, all-stock-plus-debt deal announced 26-Dec-2025 and closed 23-Apr-2026 (consolidation into Coforge's financials effective 1-May-2026 -- a FY27 event, absent from the FY26 numbers above). Encora shareholders receive equity worth ~$1.89bn, equal to ~20% of Coforge's expanded share capital -- mechanically a ~25% increase in share count for existing holders, a real and immediate dilution overhang once the preferential-allotment shares are issued. Coforge separately raised a $550M, 3-year loan at a 4.6% fixed rate to retire Encora's existing debt; total company debt is guided to rise from roughly Rs 1,500cr (FY26) to roughly Rs 4,000cr (FY27E) before flattening -- a real leverage step-up, though CRISIL's response has actually been an upgrade (long-term issuer rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Positive, short-term reaffirmed CRISIL A1+) rather than a negative-watch action, which is a materially more comfortable credit read than some recent large-cap IT M&A (contrast: Persistent-Nagarro drew an ICRA Watch Negative). Encora itself is the weaker asset in the pair: ~$600M FY26E revenue at ~19% EBITDA margin, but only ~7-10% organic growth over the trailing two years, versus Coforge's own high-teens-to-20%+ pace -- so blended reported growth mechanically dilutes as Encora consolidates in, even as the deal is guided EPS-accretive within ~18 months and management assumes only a conservative ~$20M of Year-1 cost synergies (~90bps combined EBITDA uplift modeled) rather than an aggressive number. Sell-side is net constructive but genuinely split on timing: Macquarie (Outperform, Rs 2,230), CLSA (High-Conviction Outperform, Rs 2,411) and Motilal Oswal (Buy, Rs 1,900) held or raised targets on the AI-engineering/geographic-diversification logic, while MarketsMOJO downgraded to Hold as early as Feb-2026 on 'elevated valuations and weakening technical indicators despite strong fundamentals' and other houses flagged near-term earnings-dilution and integration-execution risk explicitly.

On valuation: CMP ~Rs 1,508-1,545 (mid-Jul-2026), mcap ~Rs 67,900-68,000cr, trailing PE cited anywhere from ~39x to ~48x depending on the EPS basis used by the source (forward PE ~24.6x per GuruFocus) -- a real premium to large-cap IT (TCS/Infosys ~24-27x forward) historically justified by Coforge's much faster growth. My own read: using the 'clean' (ex-one-off-tax-credit) FY26 PAT of ~Rs 1,311.7cr against ~4.4cr shares implies clean EPS of roughly Rs 30 and a clean trailing PE closer to ~51x at CMP ~Rs 1,545 -- richer than the reported-EPS multiple once the tax artifact is removed, and that is BEFORE the ~25% Encora-driven share dilution further lowers per-share earnings in the near term (partially, not fully, offset by Encora's own EBITDA contribution). Client and vertical concentration have both drifted up: top-5 clients now ~21.8% of revenue (from 18.3%), top-10 ~31.4% (from 27.9%), and BFSI+Insurance+Travel together were ~70% of FY25 revenue (BFSI alone ~55%, Travel ~18-20%) -- a real, worth-watching concentration in vertical mix and discretionary-spend cyclicality, not yet extreme for a firm this size but trending the wrong way. GenAI pricing/deflation risk is a genuine forward overhang rather than a crystallized problem today: management frames AI (GitHub Copilot embedded through the SDLC) as a productivity tool cutting 30% of time/cost on large modernization deals, which is a genuine margin/win-rate tailwind today, but the same mechanism is the classic 'AI eats billed hours' risk if large AI vendors start selling equivalent tooling directly to enterprise clients and disintermediate the coding/testing/automation layer Coforge bills for -- not visible in the numbers yet, worth monitoring each quarter via realization/pricing commentary.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, and specifically Hold rather than Sell because there is currently no quant score for COFORGE in the STOCK_SCORECARD_750 build ("no quant row yet") -- under the V1 asymmetric-override rule the quant score is the only permitted source of a Sell call (an analyst may rescue a score-Sell to Hold, never manufacture a Sell where the score is Hold or absent), so absent a score there is no basis to issue a Sell here regardless of how rich the valuation reads. On the merits that does not feel like an artificial constraint: operating execution is genuinely strong (Sabre ramp on-track, record $1.75bn order book, broad-based deal wins, real margin expansion), the Encora deal's credit response (a CRISIL upgrade, not a negative-watch) is a more comfortable signal than peer large-cap-IT M&A of similar size, and sell-side remains net-constructive even where split. The offsetting concerns -- a materially tax-inflated FY26 EPS base, a rich clean-PE once that one-off is stripped out, a ~25% imminent Encora-driven share dilution, decelerating FY27 organic guidance (13% CC vs FY26's realized 29.2%), and rising client/vertical concentration -- argue against paying up further, but none of them individually or together rise to the 'genuine Hold-vs-Sell judgment call' bar this desk reserves for escalation (Q1 FY27 is simply not out yet to test the guidance, and the Encora credit/rating response has been constructive rather than alarming). Net: Hold, watch the 27/28-Jul-2026 Q1 FY27 print closely for whether the 13% CC guide and the >20.5-21% FY27 EBITDA margin guide are tracking, and re-underwrite once Encora's first consolidated quarter of numbers (expected Q2 FY27 onward) shows the real blended growth/margin/dilution math rather than pre-close guidance.
summary: Coforge delivered a strong FY26 (revenue +29.2% USD, EBIT margin +370bps to 14.4%, record $1.75bn order book, Sabre deal executing on-plan) but FY26 PAT growth of 91.6% was flattered by a Rs 244cr one-off deferred-tax credit (Cigniti-merger related) -- clean PAT growth is closer to 61-62%. The $2.35bn Encora acquisition (closed 23-Apr-2026, consolidating from May-2026) adds AI-engineering scale but brings a ~25% share-count dilution, a debt step-up to ~Rs 4,000cr FY27E, and a slower-growing, lower-margin acquired business, even as CRISIL's response was an upgrade to AA+/Stable rather than a negative-rating-watch. At a clean trailing PE near 51x (using ex-one-off PAT), the stock is not obviously cheap for FY27 organic guidance of just 13% constant-currency growth, and client/vertical concentration (top-10 clients 31.4% of revenue, BFSI+Travel+Insurance ~70%) is drifting up. With no quant score yet computed for this name, the only defensible call under V1 rules is Hold -- watch the 27/28-Jul-2026 Q1 FY27 print for the first real read on both the growth guide and Encora's blended-in numbers.
positive_para: FY26 revenue grew 29.2% YoY in USD with EBIT margin expanding 370bps to 14.4% (Q4FY26 EBIT margin 16.6%, EBITDA margin 20.6%, both records), and the company enters FY27 with a record $1.75bn executable order book built on broad-based, multi-vertical deal wins (BFSI/healthcare/travel/Govt/insurance), not client concentration. The Sabre mega-deal -- the single largest swing factor in recent growth -- is executing ahead of cost plan per management commentary, a genuine delivery/execution positive rather than just a revenue number. The $2.35bn Encora acquisition adds real AI-engineering scale (combined ~$2.5bn revenue ambition) and diversifies the business, and CRISIL's rating response to the deal was an UPGRADE to AA+/Stable (from AA/Positive) rather than a negative watch -- a materially more comfortable credit read than comparable large-cap-IT M&A this cycle. Sell-side remains net constructive (Macquarie Outperform Rs 2,230, CLSA High-Conviction Outperform Rs 2,411, Motilal Oswal Buy Rs 1,900), and management guides the deal EPS-accretive within ~18 months on even conservative (~$20M) synergy assumptions.
negative_para: FY26's headline 91.6% PAT growth is partly a tax-line artifact: a Rs 244cr deferred-tax credit (Rs 153cr in Q4 alone) tied to Cigniti-merger DTA/DTL reversal inflates reported earnings versus a clean ~61-62% PAT growth rate, and management itself guides the effective tax rate normalizing back to 23-24% in FY27-28, meaning FY27 reported profit growth optically decelerates even before any Encora effect. The Encora deal brings a ~25% imminent increase in share count (Encora holders take ~20% of expanded capital), a debt step-up from ~Rs 1,500cr to ~Rs 4,000cr guided FY27E, and a materially slower/lower-margin acquired business (~7-10% organic growth, ~19% EBITDA margin vs Coforge's own high-teens-to-20%+ growth) that will mechanically dilute blended growth as it consolidates from May-2026. On a clean (ex-one-off) EPS basis the stock trades near ~51x trailing earnings against FY27 organic guidance of just 13% constant-currency growth -- not a cheap combination -- and client/vertical concentration is drifting up (top-5 clients 21.8% vs 18.3% prior, top-10 31.4% vs 27.9%; BFSI+Insurance+Travel ~70% of FY25 revenue), leaving real discretionary-spend cyclicality exposure. GenAI-driven pricing/deflation is a genuine forward risk if large AI vendors sell equivalent tooling directly to clients, even though it is a productivity tailwind today. Q1 FY27 results (due 27/28-Jul-2026) are not yet out, so the 13% CC guide is entirely unverified as of this review.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At CMP ~Rs 1,508-1,545 (mcap ~Rs 67,900-68,000cr, mid-Jul-2026), reported trailing PE is cited anywhere from ~39x to ~48x depending on source EPS basis; forward PE is ~24.6x per GuruFocus. My own estimate: using 'clean' FY26 PAT (Rs 1,555.7cr reported minus the Rs 244cr one-off deferred-tax credit = ~Rs 1,311.7cr) against ~4.4cr shares gives clean EPS of roughly Rs 30 and a clean trailing PE closer to ~51x -- richer than most reported-EPS multiples in circulation, and this is before the ~25% Encora-driven share-count dilution further pressures per-share earnings near-term (partially offset by Encora's own EBITDA contribution once consolidated). Sustaining a ~40-50x multiple (on either basis) requires the market to underwrite continued high-teens-to-20%+ blended growth for several years; FY27 organic guidance of just 13% constant-currency growth, plus a slower-growing (~7-10% organic) Encora blending in from May-2026, makes that a harder underwrite than the FY26 print alone would suggest, even granting Coforge's real history of beating its own initial guidance. Fair value on a normalized ~15-16% three-to-five-year blended growth view (Sabre ramp normalizing, Encora drag partly offset by cross-sell/AI-engineering demand, margin near the FY27 >20.5-21% EBITDA guide) sits meaningfully below the current clean multiple -- but not so far below, nor the credit/leverage story so alarming (CRISIL upgraded, not negative-watch), as to justify a Sell call absent an actual quant score and with Q1 FY27 (the first real test of the 13% guide) still four working days from release as of this review.
